<r>℣.</r> Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos: quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu ejus sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.

3dee797156:
<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>N</c>octe surgéntes vigilémus omnes,
Semper in psalmis meditémur, atque
Víribus totis Dómino canámus
Dúlciter hymnos.

<h>U</h>t pio Regi páriter canéntes,
Cum suis Sanctis mereámur aulam
Íngredi cæli, simul et beátam
Dúcere vitam.

<h>P</h>ræstet hoc nobis Déitas beáta
Patris, ac Nati, paritérque Sancti
Spíritus, cujus réboat per omnem
Glória mundum.
Amen.
7798d5e712:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>N</c>ow, from the slumbers of the night arising,
Chant we the holy psalmody of David,
Hymns to our Master, with a voice concordant,
Sweetly intoning.

<h>S</h>o may our Monarch pitifully hear us,
That we may merit with his saints to enter
Mansions eternal, therewithal possessing
Joy beatific.

<h>T</h>his be our portion, God forever blessed,
Father eternal, Son, and Holy Spirit,
Whose is the glory, which through all creation
Ever resoundeth.
Amen.

0638ce2c25:
<h>Te Deum</h>
<r>Canticum SS. Ambrosii et Augustini</r>
<c>T</c>e Deum laudámus: * te Dóminum confitémur.
Te ætérnum Patrem * omnis terra venerátur.
Tibi omnes Ángeli, * tibi Cæli, et univérsæ Potestátes:
Tibi Chérubim et Séraphim * incessábili voce proclámant:
<n>(Fit reverentia)</n> Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus * Dóminus Deus Sábaoth.
Pleni sunt cæli et terra * majestátis glóriæ tuæ.
Te gloriósus * Apostolórum chorus,
Te Prophetárum * laudábilis númerus,
Te Mártyrum candidátus * laudat exércitus.
Te per orbem terrárum * sancta confitétur Ecclésia,
Patrem * imménsæ majestátis;
Venerándum tuum verum * et únicum Fílium;
Sanctum quoque * Paráclitum Spíritum.
Tu Rex glóriæ, * Christe.
Tu Patris * sempitérnus es Fílius.
<n>(Fit reverentia)</n> Tu, ad liberándum susceptúrus hóminem: * non horruísti Vírginis úterum.
Tu, devícto mortis acúleo, * aperuísti credéntibus regna cælórum.
Tu ad déxteram Dei sedes, * in glória Patris.
Judex créderis * esse ventúrus.
<n>(Sequens versus dicitur flexis genibus)</n> Te ergo quǽsumus, tuis fámulis súbveni, * quos pretióso sánguine redemísti.
Ætérna fac cum Sanctis tuis * in glória numerári.
Salvum fac pópulum tuum, Dómine, * et bénedic hereditáti tuæ.
Et rege eos, * et extólle illos usque in ætérnum.
Per síngulos dies * benedícimus te.
<n>(Fit reverentia, secundum consuetudinem)</n> Et laudámus nomen tuum in sǽculum, * et in sǽculum sǽculi.
Dignáre, Dómine, die isto * sine peccáto nos custodíre.
Miserére nostri, Dómine, * miserére nostri.
Fiat misericórdia tua, Dómine, super nos, * quemádmodum sperávimus in te.
In te, Dómine, sperávi: * non confúndar in ætérnum.
6dd1763062:
<h>Te Deum</h>
<c>W</c>e praise thee, O God, * we acknowledge thee to be the Lord.
All the earth doth worship thee, * the Father everlasting.
To thee all Angels cry aloud, * the Heavens, and all the Powers therein.
To thee Cherubim and Seraphim * continually do cry.
<n>bow head</n> Holy, Holy, Holy * Lord God of Sabaoth;
Heaven and earth are full * of the Majesty of thy glory.
The glorious company of the Apostles * praise thee.
The goodly fellowship of the Prophets * praise thee.
The noble army of Martyrs * praise thee.
The holy Church throughout all the world * doth acknowledge thee;
The Father, * of an infinite Majesty.
Thine honourable, true, * and only Son;
Also the Holy Ghost, * the Comforter.
Thou art the King of Glory, * O Christ.
Thou art the everlasting * Son of the Father.
<n>During the following verse all make a profound bow:</n> When thou tookest upon thee to deliver man, * thou didst not abhor the Virgin's womb.
When thou hadst overcome the sharpness of death, * thou didst open the Kingdom of Heaven to all believers.
Thou sittest at the right hand of God, * in the glory of the Father.
We believe that thou shalt come * to be our Judge.
<n>Kneel for the following verse</n> We therefore pray thee, help thy servants, * whom thou hast redeemed with thy precious Blood.
Make them to be numbered with thy Saints, * in glory everlasting.
O Lord, save thy people, * and bless thine heritage.
Govern them, * and lift them up for ever.
Day by day * we magnify thee;
<n>During the following verse, by local custom, all make a profound bow.</n> And we worship thy Name * ever, world without end.
Vouchsafe, O Lord, to keep us * this day without sin.
O Lord, have mercy upon us, * have mercy upon us.
O Lord, let thy mercy lighten upon us, * as our trust is in thee.
O Lord, in thee have I trusted, * let me never be confounded.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>L</c>ucis Creátor óptime,
Lucem diérum próferens,
Primórdiis lucis novæ,
Mundi parans oríginem:

<h>Q</h>ui mane iunctum vésperi
Diem vocári prǽcipis:
Tetrum chaos illábitur,
Audi preces cum flétibus.

<h>N</h>e mens graváta crímine,
Vitæ sit exsul múnere,
Dum nil perénne cógitat,
Seséque culpis ílligat.

Vitále tollat prǽmium:
Vitémus omne nóxium:
Purgémus omne péssimum.

Patríque compar Únice,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito
Regnans per omne sǽculum.

<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>O</c> blest Creator of the light,
Who mak’st the day with radiance bright,
And o’er the forming world didst call
The light from chaos first of all;

<h>W</h>hose wisdom joined in meet array
The morn and eve, and named them day:
Night comes with all its darkling fears;
Regard thy people’s prayers and tears.

<h>L</h>est, sunk in sin, and whelmed with strife,
They lose the gift of endless life;
While thinking but the thoughts of time,
They weave new chains of woe and crime.

<h>B</h>ut grant them grace that they may strain
The heavenly gate and prize to gain:
Each harmful lure aside to cast,
And purge away each error past.

<h>O</h> Father, that we ask be done,
Through Jesus Christ, thine only Son;
Who, with the Holy Ghost and thee,
Doth live and reign eternally.
Amen.

Hostémque nostrum cómprime,

That with thy wonted favor thou
Wouldst be our guard and keeper now.

From nightly fears and fantasies;
Tread under foot our ghostly foe,
That no pollution we may know.

Through Jesus Christ, thine only Son;
Who, with the Holy Ghost and thee,
Doth live and reign eternally.

<n>After the blessing the Salve Regina is begun by two cantors (on Doubles and Totum Duplex) or by one; at its beginning all prostrate, or kneel in Paschaltide, until "Salve Regina" has been sung; then the procession goes into the church and the Hebdomadarian sprinkles the brethren with holy water.</n>
<r>Ant.</r> Salve, Regína, mater misericórdiæ: Vita, dulcédo et spes nostra, salve. Ad te clamámus éxsules fílii Hevæ. Ad te suspirámus, geméntes et flentes in hac lacrimárum valle. <r>Ant.</r> O lumen Ecclésiæ, Doctor veritátis, Rosa patiéntiæ, Ebur castitátis, Aquam sapiéntiæ propinásti gratis: Prædicátor grátiæ, nos junge beátis.

<h>Procession at the end of Compline</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Hail, holy Queen, Mother of mercy, our life, our sweetness and our hope. To thee do we cry, poor banished children of Eve; to thee do we send up our sighs, mourning and weeping in this valley of tears. Turn then, most gracious advocate, thine eyes of mercy toward us; and after this our exile show unto us the blessed fruit of thy womb, Jesus. O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary.
<r>℣.</r> Make me worthy to praise thee, holy Virgin.
<r>℟.</r> Give me strength against thine enemies.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>G</c>rant, we beseech thee, O Lord God, that we thy servants may enjoy perpetual health of mind and body; and by the glorious intercession of blessed Mary ever Virgin, be delivered from present sorrow and enjoy eternal gladness. Through Christ our Lord.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Ant.</r> O light of the Church, teacher of truth, rose of patience, ivory of chastity, freely thou didst pour forth the waters of wisdom: preacher of grace, unite us with the blessed.
<r>℣.</r> Pray for us, blessed Father Dominic.
<r>℟.</r> That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>G</c>rant, we beseech thee, almighty God, that we who are weighed down by the burden of our sins may be raised up by the patronage of blessed Dominic, thy Confessor, our Father. Through Christ our Lord.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>℣.</r> May the souls of the faithful, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<c>N</c>ow in the sun's new dawning ray,
Lowly of heart, our God we pray
That he from harm may keep us free
In all the deeds this day shall see.

<h>M</h>ay fear of him our tongues restrain,
Lest strife unguarded speech should stain:
His favouring care our guardian be,
Lest our eyes feed on vanity.

<h>M</h>ay every heart be pure from sin
And folly find no place therein:
Scant need of food, excess denied,
Wear down in us the body's pride.

<h>T</h>hat when the light of day is gone,
And night in course shall follow on.
We, free from cares the world affords,
May chant the praise that is our Lord's.

<h>A</h>ll laud to God the Father be,
All praise, Eternal Son, to thee:
All glory, as is ever meet,
To God the holy Paraclete.
Amen.

<r>Rom 13</r>
<c>N</c>ox præcéssit, dies autem appropinquávit. Abjiciámus ergo ópera tenebrárum, et induámur arma lucis. Sicut in die honéste ambulémus.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>E</c>cce jam noctis tenuátur umbra,
Lucis auróra rútilans corúscat:
Nísibus totis rogitémus omnes
Cunctipoténtem:

<h>U</h>t Deus nostri miserátus, omnem
Pellat languórem, tríbuat salútem,
Donet et nobis pietáte Patris
Regna polorum.

<h>P</h>ræstet hoc nobis Déitas beáta
Patris, ac Nati, paritérque Sancti
Spíritus, cujus réboat in omni
Glória mundo.

<r>℟.</r> Quia fuísti adjútor meus.
80521aec91:

<r>Rom 13</r>
<c>T</c>he night is passed, and the day is at hand. Let us therefore cast off the works of darkness, and put on the armour of light. Let us walk honestly, as in the day.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>L</c>o, the dim shadows of the night are waning;
Lightsome and blushing, dawn of day returneth;
Fervent in spirit, to the world’s Creator
Pray we devoutly:

<h>T</h>hat he may pity sinners in their sighing,
Banish all troubles, kindly health bestowing;
And may he grant us, of his countless blessings,
Peace that is endless.

<h>T</h>his be our portion, God forever blessed,
Father eternal, Son, and Holy Spirit,
Whose is the glory, which through all creation
Ever resoundeth.
Amen.

<r>℟.</r> Quia fuísti adjútor meus.

<h>Invitatorium</h>
<n>Quo dicto, séquitur:</n>
<r>℣.</r> Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, jubilémus Deo salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem ejus in confessióne, et in psalmis jubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> In manu tua, Dómine, * Omnes fines terræ.
<r>℣.</r> Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos: quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu ejus sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Omnes fines terræ.
<r>℣.</r> Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus ejus: <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos: quia ipse est Dóminus Deus noster: nos autem pópulus ejus, et oves páscuæ ejus.
<r>Ant.</r> In manu tua, Dómine, * Omnes fines terræ.
<r>℣.</r> Hódie, si vocem ejus audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt, et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Omnes fines terræ.
<r>℣.</r> Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde: ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus jurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> In manu tua, Dómine, * Omnes fines terræ.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Omnes fines terræ.
<r>Ant.</r> In manu tua, Dómine, * Omnes fines terræ.

d43afe2c5e:
<h>Invitatorium</h>
<n>Quo dicto, séquitur:</n>
<r>℣.</r> Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, jubilémus Deo salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem ejus in confessióne, et in psalmis jubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Dóminum Deum nostrum * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos: quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu ejus sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus ejus: <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos: quia ipse est Dóminus Deus noster: nos autem pópulus ejus, et oves páscuæ ejus.
<r>Ant.</r> Dóminum Deum nostrum * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Hódie, si vocem ejus audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt, et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde: ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus jurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Dóminum Deum nostrum * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Dóminum Deum nostrum * Veníte, adorémus.

d2b86ab13b:
<h>Capitulum Hymnus Versus</h>
<r>2 Cor 1</r>
<c>B</c>enedíctus Deus et Pater Dómini nostri Jesu Christi, Pater misericordiárum, et Deus totíus consolatiónis, qui consolátur nos in omni tribulatióne nostra.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>O</c> lux beáta Trínitas,
Et principális Únitas,
Jam sol recédit ígneus,
Infúnde lumen córdibus.

<h>T</h>e mane laudum cármine,
Te deprecémur véspere:
Te nostra supplex glória
Per cuncta laudet sǽcula.

<h>D</h>eo Patri sit glória,
Ejúsque soli Fílio,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
Et nunc, et in perpétuum.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Vespertína orátio ascéndat ad te, Dómine.
<r>℟.</r> Et descéndat super nos misericórdia tua.
b11e3cd0ea:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>2 Cor 1</r>
<c>B</c>lessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort, who comforteth us in all our tribulation.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>O</c> Trinity of blessed Light,
O Unity of sovereign might,
as now the fiery sun departs,
shed Thou Thy beams within our hearts.

<h>T</h>o Thee our morning song of praise,
to Thee our evening prayer we raise;
Thee may our glory evermore
in lowly reverence adore.

<h>A</h>ll laud to God the Father be;
all praise, Eternal Son, to Thee;
all glory, as is ever meet,
to God the Holy Paraclete.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Let the evening prayer ascend unto thee, O Lord.
<r>℟.</r> And let there descend upon us thy mercy.
fafa608ba9:
<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>V</c>erbum supérnum, pródiens
A Patre olim éxiens,
Qui natus orbi súbvenis,
Cursu declívi témporis.

<h>I</h>llúmina nunc péctora,
Tuóque amóre cóncrema;
Audíto ut præcónio
Sint pulsa tandem lúbrica.

<h>I</h>udéxque cum post áderis
Rimári facta péctoris,
Reddens vicem pro ábditis,
Iustísque regnum pro bonis.

<h>N</h>on demum arctémur malis
Pro qualitáte críminis;
Sed cum beátis cómpotes
Simus perénnes cælibes.

<h>L</h>aus, honor, virtus, glória,
Deo Patri, et Fílio,
Sancto simul Paráclito,
In sæculórum sǽcula.
Amen.
316493f49a:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>C</c>elestial Word, to this our earth
Sent down from God's eternal clime,
To save mankind by mortal birth
Into a world of change and time;

<h>E</h>nlighten our hearts; vain hopes destroy;
And in thy love's consuming fire
Fill all the soul with heavenly joy,
And melt the dross of low desire.

<h>S</h>o when the Judge of quick and dead
Shall bid his awful summons come,
To whelm the guilty soul with dread,
And call the blessed to their home.

<h>S</h>aved from the whirling, black abyss,
Forevermore to us be given
To share the feast of saintly bliss,
And see the face of God in heaven.

<h>T</h>o God the Father and the Son
Our songs with one accord we raise;
And to the Holy Spirit, One
With them, be ever equal praise
Amen.

<h>Capitulum Hymnus Versus</h>
<r>Jer 23</r>
<c>E</c>cce dies véniunt, dicit Dóminus, et suscitábo David germen justum: et regnábit rex, et sápiens erit: et fáciet judícium et justítiam in terra.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>V</c>ox clara ecce íntonat,
Obscúra quæque íncrepat:
Pellántur éminus sómnia;
Ab æthre Christus prómicat.

<h>M</h>ens jam resúrgat tórpida
Quæ sorde exstat sáucia;
Sidus refúlget jam novum,
Ut tollat omne nóxium.

<h>E</h> sursum Agnus míttitur
Laxáre gratis débitum:
Omnes pro indulgéntia
Vocem demus cum lácrimis,

<h>S</h>ecúndo ut cum fúlserit,
Mundúmque horror cínxerit,
Non pro reátu púniat,
Sed nos pius tunc prótegat.

<h>L</h>aus, honor, virtus, glória,
Deo Patri, et Fílio,
Sancto simul Paráclito,
In sæculórum sǽcula.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Vox clamántis in desérto.
<r>℟.</r> Paráte viam Dómini.
befeef17a3:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>Jer 23</r>
<c>B</c>ehold the days come, saith the Lord, and I will raise up to David a just branch: and a king shall reign, and shall be wise, and shall execute judgement and justice in the earth.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>H</c>ark, a herald voice is calling;
“Christ is nigh,” it seems to say;
“Cast away the dreams of darkness,
O ye children of the day.”

<h>S</h>tartled at the solemn warning,
Let the earth-bound soul arise;
Christ, her sun, all sloth dispelling,
Shines upon the morning skies.

<h>L</h>o, the Lamb, so long expected,
Comes with pardon down from heaven;
Let us haste, with tears of sorrow,
One and all to be forgiven.

<h>S</h>o when next he comes with glory,
Wrapping all the earth in fear,
May he then as our defender
On the clouds of heaven appear.

<h>H</h>onour, glory, virtue, merit,
To the Father and the Son,
With the co-eternal Spirit,
While eternal ages run.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Vox clamántis in desérto.
<r>℟.</r> Paráte viam Dómini.

<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>C</c>ónditor alme síderum,
Ætérna lux credéntium,
Christe, Redémptor ómnium,
Exáudi preces súpplicum.

<h>Q</h>ui cóndolens intéritu
Mortis períre sǽculum,
Salvásti mundum lánguidum,
Donans reis remédium,

<h>V</h>ergénte mundi véspere,
Uti sponsus de thálamo,
Egréssus honestíssima
Vírginis matris cláusula.

<h>C</h>uius forti poténtiæ
Genu curvántur ómnia;
Cæléstia, terréstria
Nutu faténtur súbdita.

<h>T</h>e deprecámur, hágie,
Ventúre judex sǽculi,
Consérva nos in témpore
Hostis a telo pérfidi.

<h>L</h>aus, honor, virtus, glória,
Deo Patri, et Fílio,
Sancto simul Paráclito,
In sæculórum sǽcula.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Roráte, cæli, désuper, et nubes pluant justum.
<r>℟.</r> Aperiátur terra, et gérminet Salvatórem.
aa969db086:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>Jer 23</r>
<c>B</c>ehold the days come, saith the Lord, and I will raise up to David a just branch: and a king shall reign, and shall be wise, and shall execute judgement and justice in the earth.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>B</c>right builder of the heavenly poles,
Eternal light of faithful souls,
Jesus, Redeemer of mankind,
Our humble prayers vouchsafe to mind.

<h>W</h>ho, lest the fraud of hell’s black king
Should all men to destruction bring,
Didst, by an act of generous love,
The fainting world’s physician prove.

<h>W</h>ho, that thou mightst our ransom pay
And wash the stains of sin away,
Wouldst from a Virgin’s womb proceed
And on the cross a victim bleed.

<h>W</h>hose glorious power, whose saving name
No sooner any voice can frame,
But heaven and earth and hell agree
To honour them with trembling knee.

<h>T</h>hee, Christ, who at the latter day
Shalt be our Judge, we humbly pray
Such arms of heavenly grace to send
As may thy Church from foes defend.

<h>B</h>e glory given and honour done
To God the Father and the Son
And to the Holy Ghost on high,
From age to age eternally.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Drop down dew, ye heavens, from above, and let the clouds rain the Just.
<r>℟.</r> Let the earth be opened, and bud forth the Saviour.

76fd840c99:
<h>Capitulum Hymnus Versus</h>
<r>Apoc 7</r>
<c>B</c>enedíctio, et cláritas, et sapiéntia, et gratiárum áctio, honor, virtus, et fortitúdo Deo nostro in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>E</c>cce jam noctis tenuátur umbra,
Lucis auróra rútilans corúscat:
Nísibus totis rogitémus omnes
Cunctipoténtem:

<h>U</h>t Deus nostri miserátus, omnem
Pellat languórem, tríbuat salútem,
Donet et nobis pietáte Patris
Regna polorum.

<h>P</h>ræstet hoc nobis Déitas beáta
Patris, ac Nati, paritérque Sancti
Spíritus, cujus réboat in omni
Glória mundo.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Dómine, refúgium factus es nobis.
<r>℟.</r> A generatióne et progénie.
fee4574b39:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>Apoc 7</r>
<c>B</c>enediction, and glory, and wisdom, and thanksgiving, honour, and power, and strength to our God for ever and ever. Amen.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>L</c>o, the dim shadows of the night are waning;
Lightsome and blushing, dawn of day returneth;
Fervent in spirit, to the world’s Creator
Pray we devoutly:

<h>T</h>hat he may pity sinners in their sighing,
Banish all troubles, kindly health bestowing;
And may he grant us, of his countless blessings,
Peace that is endless.

<h>T</h>his be our portion, God forever blessed,
Father eternal, Son, and Holy Spirit,
Whose is the glory, which through all creation
Ever resoundeth.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Lord, thou hast been our refuge.
<r>℟.</r> From generation to generation.

d5c144b408:
<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>C</c>hriste, qui lux es et dies,
Noctis tenébras détegis,
Lucísque lumen créderis,
Lumen beátum prǽdicans.

<h>P</h>recámur sancte Dómine,
defénde nos in hac nocte:
Sit nobis in te réquies,
Quiétam noctem tríbue.

<h>N</h>e gravis somnus írruat,
Nec hostis nos subrípiat,
Nec caro illi conséntiens
Nos tibi reos státuat.

<h>O</h>culi somnum cápiant,
Cor ad te semper vígilet:
Déxtera tua prótegat
Fámulos, qui te díligunt.

<h>D</h>efénsor noster áspice,
Insidiántes réprime,
Gubérna tuos fámulos,
<n>Ad hunc Vers. genuflectatur</n>
Quos Sánguine mercátus es.

<h>M</h>eménto nostri, Dómine,
In gravi isto córpore:
Qui es defénsor ánimæ,
Adésto nobis, Dómine.

<h>P</h>ræsta Pater omnípotens,
Per Jesum Christum Dóminum,
Qui tecum in perpétuum
Regnat cum Sancto Spíritu.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Custódi nos, Dómine, ut pupíllam óculi.
<r>℟.</r> Sub umbra alárum tuárum prótege nos.
55d7f86db9:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>C</c>hriste, qui lux es et dies,
Thou dost lay bare the darkness of night,
And art believed the light of light,
Proclaiming the blessed light.

We pray thee, holy Lord,
defénde nos in hac nocte:
Sit nobis in te réquies,
Grant us a quiet night.

<h>N</h>e gravis somnus írruat,
Nec hostis nos subrípiat,
Nec caro illi conséntiens
Nos tibi reos státuat.

<h>O</h>culi somnum cápiant,
Cor ad te semper vígilet:
May thy right hand protect
The servants that love thee.

Look upon us, our Defender,
Hold back them that lie in wait,
Govern thy servants,
<n>Ad hunc Vers. genuflectatur</n>
Whom thou hast purchased with thy Blood.

Remember us, O Lord,
In gravi isto córpore:
Thou who art the defender of the soul,
Be present with us, O Lord.

<h>P</h>ræsta Pater omnípotens,
Per Jesum Christum Dóminum,
Qui tecum in perpétuum
Regnat cum Sancto Spíritu.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Keep us, O Lord, as the apple of thine eye.
<r>℟.</r> Protect us under the shadow of thy wings.

e031ad0334:
<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>S</c>ummi largítor prǽmii,
Spes qui es única mundi,
Preces inténde servórum,
Ad te devóte clamántium.

<h>N</h>ostra te consciéntia
Grave offendísse monstra:
Quam emúndes, supplicámus,
Ab ómnibus piáculis.

<h>S</h>i rénuis, quis tríbuet?
Indúlge, quia potens es:
Te corde rogáre mundo
Fac nos precámur, Dómine.

<h>E</h>rgo nunc accépta nostrum,
Qui sacrásti jejúnium:
Quo mýstice paschália
Capiámus sacraménta.

<h>S</h>umma nobis hoc cónferat
In Deitáte Trínitas:
In qua gloriátur unus
Per cuncta sǽcula Deus.
Amen.
e6c3bd05ee:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>T</c>he fast, as taught by holy lore,
We keep in solemn course once more:
The fast to all men known, and bound
In forty days of yearly round.

<h>T</h>he law and seers that were of old
In diverse ways this Lent foretold,
Which Christ, all seasons’ King and Guide,
In after ages sanctified.

<h>M</h>ore sparing therefore let us make
The words we speak, the food we take,
Our sleep and mirth, —and closer barred
Be every sense in holy guard.

<h>A</h>void the evil thoughts that roll
Like waters o’er the heedless soul;
Nor let the foe occasion find
Our souls in slavery to bind.

<h>I</h>n prayer together let us fall,
And cry for mercy, one and all,
And weep before the Judge’s feet,
And his avenging wrath entreat.

<h>T</h>hy grace have we offended sore,
By sins, O God, which we deplore;
But pour upon us from on high,
O pardoning One, thy clemency.

<h>R</h>emember thou, though frail we be,
That yet thine handiwork are we;
Nor let the honour of thy name
Be by another put to shame.

<h>F</h>orgive the sin that we have wrought;
Increase the good that we have sought:
That we at length, our wanderings o'er,
May please thee here and evermore.

<h>G</h>rant O thou Blessed Trinity,
Grant, O Essential Unity,
That this our fast of forty days
May work our profit and thy praise.
Amen.

876250b527:
<h>Capitulum Hymnus Versus</h>
<r>2 Cor 6</r>
<c>H</c>ortámur vos, ne in vácuum grátiam Dei recipiátis. Ait enim: Témpore accépto exaudívi te, et in die salútis adjúvi te.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>I</c>am Christe sol justítiæ,
Mentis diéscant ténebræ:
Virtútum ut lux rédeat,
Terris diem cum réparas.

<h>D</h>ans tempus acceptábile,
Et pǽnitens cor tríbue,
Convértat ut benígnitas
Quos longa suffert píetas.

<h>Q</h>uiddámque pæniténtiæ
Da ferre, quamvis grávium,
Majóre tuo múnere,
Quo démptio fit críminum.

<h>D</h>ies venit, dies tua,
In qua reflórent ómnia:
Lætémur in hac ad tuam
Per hanc redúcti grátiam.

<h>T</h>e rerum univérsitas,
Clemens, adóret, Trínitas,
Et nos novi per véniam,
Novum canámus cánticum.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Scuto circúmdabit te véritas ejus.
<r>℟.</r> Non timébis a timóre noctúrno.
e3561d2166:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>2 Cor 6</r>
<c>H</c>ortámur vos, ne in vácuum grátiam Dei recipiátis. Ait enim: Témpore accépto exaudívi te, et in die salútis adjúvi te.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>J</c>esu, salvation’s Sun Divine,
Within our inmost bosoms shine,
With light all darkness drive away
And give the world a better day.

<h>N</h>ow days of grace with mercy flow,
O Lord, the gift of tears bestow,
To wash our stains in every part,
Whilst heavenly fire consumes the heart.

<h>R</h>ise, crystal tears, from that same source
From whence our sins derive their course;
Nor cease, till hardened hearts relent,
And softened by your streams, repent.

<h>B</h>ehold, the happy days return,
The days of joy for them that mourn;
May we of their indulgence share,
And bless the God that grants our prayer.

<h>M</h>ay heaven and earth aloud proclaim
The Trinity’s almighty fame;
And we, restored to grace, rejoice
In newness both of heart and voice.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> His truth shall compass thee with a shield.
<r>℟.</r> Thou shalt not be afraid of the terror of the night.
b2802d98f3:
<h>Capitulum Hymnus Versus</h>
<r>2 Cor 6</r>
<c>H</c>ortámur vos, ne in vácuum grátiam Dei recipiátis. Ait enim: Témpore accépto exaudívi te, et in die salútis adjúvi te.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>A</c>udi, benígne Cónditor,
Nostras preces cum flétibus,
In hoc sacro jejúnio
Fusas quadragenário.

<h>S</h>crutátor alme córdium,
Infírma tu scis vírium:
Ad te revérsis éxhibe
Remissiónis grátiam.

<h>M</h>ultum quidem peccávimus,
Sed parce confiténtibus:
Ad laudem tui nóminis
Confer medélam lánguidis.

<h>S</h>ic corpus extra cónteri
Dona per abstinéntiam,
Ieiúnet ut mens sóbria
A labe prorsus críminum.

<h>P</h>ræsta, beáta Trínitas,
Concéde, simplex Únitas;
Ut fructuósa sint tuis
Ieiuniórum múnera.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Ángelis suis Deus mandávit de te.
<r>℟.</r> Ut custódiant te in ómnibus viis tuis.
e99c800f8e:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>2 Cor 6</r>
<c>H</c>ortámur vos, ne in vácuum grátiam Dei recipiátis. Ait enim: Témpore accépto exaudívi te, et in die salútis adjúvi te.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>O</c> kind Creator, bow thine ear
To mark the cry, to know the tear
Before thy throne of mercy spent
In this thy holy fast of Lent.

<h>O</h>ur hearts are open, Lord, to thee:
Thou knowest our infirmity;
Pour out on all who seek thy face
Abundance of thy pardoning grace.

<h>O</h>ur sins are many, this we know;
Spare us, good Lord, thy mercy show;
And for the honour of thy name
Our fainting souls to life reclaim.

<h>G</h>ive us the self-control that springs
From discipline of outward things,
That fasting inward secretly
The soul may purely dwell with thee.

<h>W</h>e pray thee, Holy Trinity,
One God, unchanging Unity,
That we from this our abstinence
May reap the fruits of penitence.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> For he hath given his angels charge over thee.
<r>℟.</r> To keep thee in all thy ways.

2b7230db6c:
<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>P</c>ange, lingua, gloriósi
Prœlium certáminis,
Et super Crucis trophǽo
Dic triúmphum nóbilem,
Quáliter Redémptor orbis
Immolátus vícerit.

<h>D</h>e paréntis protoplásti
Fraude Factor cóndolens,
Quando pomi noxiális
Morsu in mortem córruit,
Ipse lignum tunc notávit,
Damna ligni ut sólveret.

<h>H</h>oc opus nostræ salútis
Ordo depopóscerat,
Multifórmis proditóris
Ars ut artem fálleret,
Et medélam ferret inde,
Hostis unde lǽserat.

<h>Q</h>uando venit ergo sacri
Plenitúdo témporis,
Missus est ab arce Patris
Natus, orbis Cónditor,
Atque ventre virgináli
Carne amíctus pródiit.

<h>V</h>agit infans inter arcta
Cónditus præsépia:
Membra pannis involúta
Virgo Mater álligat:
Et manus, pedésque, et crura
Stricta cingit fáscia.

<h>G</h>lória, et honor Deo
Usqueqáque Altíssimo,
Una Patri, Filióque;
Inclyto Paráclito:
Cui laus est et potéstas,
Per ætérna sǽcula.
Amen.
58ff6dd241:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>S</c>ing, my tongue, the glorious battle
Sing the last, the dread affray;
O'er the cross, the victor's trophy,
Sound the high triumphal lay:
Tell how Christ, the world's Redeemer,
As a victim won the day.

<h>G</h>od, his Maker, sorely grieving
That the first-made Adam fell,
When he ate the fruit of sorrow,
Whose reward was death and hell,
Noted then this wood, the ruin
Of the ancient wood to quell.

<h>F</h>or the work of our salvation
Needs would have his order so,
And the multiform deceiver's
Art by art would overthrow,
And from thence would bring the med'cine
Whence the insult of the foe.

<h>W</h>herefore, when the sacred fullness
Of the appointed time was come,
This world's Maker left his Father,
Sent the heav'nly mansion from,
And proceeded, God Incarnate,
Of the Virgin's holy womb.

<h>W</h>eeps the infant in the manger
That in Bethlehem's stable stands;
And his limbs the Virgin Mother
Doth compose in swaddling bands,
Meetly thus in linen folding
Of her God the feet and hands.

<h>T</h>o the Trinity be glory
Everlasting, as is meet;
Equal to the Father, equal
To the Son, and Paraclete:
Trinal Unity, whose praises
All created things repeat.
Amen.

f005d4754f:
<h>Capitulum Hymnus Versus</h>
<r>Jer 11</r>
<c>T</c>u autem, Dómine Sábaoth, qui júdicas juste, et probas renes et corda, vídeam ultiónem tuam ex eis: tibi enim revelávi causam meam, Dómine Deus meus.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>L</c>ustris sex qui jam peráctis,
Tempus implens córporis,
Se volénte natus ad hoc,
Passióni déditus,
Agnus in Crucis levátur
Immolándus stípite.

<h>H</h>ic acétum, fel, arúndo,
Sputa, clavi, láncea:
Mite corpus perforátur,
Sanguis, unda prófluit:
Terra, pontus, astra, mundus,
Quo lavántur flúmine!

<h>C</h>rux fidélis, inter omnes
Arbor una nóbilis:
Nulla silva talem profert
Fronde, flore, gérmine:
Dulce lignum, dulces clavos,
Dulce pondus sústinet.

<h>F</h>lecte ramos, arbor alta,
Tensa laxa víscera,
Et rigor lentéscat ille,
Quem dedit natívitas:
Ut supérni membra Regis
Miti tendas stípite.

<h>S</h>ola digna tu fuísti
Ferre sæcli prétium,
Atque portum præparáre
Nauta mundo náufrago,
Quem sacer cruor perúnxit,
Fusus Agni córpore.

<h>G</h>lória et honor Deo
Usquequáque altíssimo:
Una Patri, Filióque,
Inclyto Paráclito:
Cui laus est et potéstas
Per ætérna sǽcula.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Éripe me de inimícis meis, Deus meus.
<r>℟.</r> Et ab insurgéntibus in me líbera me.
2d40ddc30d:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>Jer 11</r>
<c>B</c>ut thou, O Lord of Sabaoth, who judgest justly, and triest the reins and hearts, let me see thy revenge on them: for to thee I have revealed my cause, O Lord my God.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>T</c>hirty years among us dwelling,
His appointed time fulfilled,
Born for this, he meets his passion,
For that this he freely willed:
On the cross the Lamb is lifted,
Where his life-blood shall be spilled.

<h>H</h>e endured the nails, the spitting,
Vinegar, and spear, and reed;
From that holy body broken
Blood and water forth proceed:
Earth, and stars, and sky, and ocean,
By that flood from stain are free.

<h>F</h>aithful cross! above all other,
One and only noble tree!
None in foliage, none in blossom,
None in fruit thy peers may be;
Sweetest wood and sweetest iron!
Sweetest weight is hung on thee.

<h>B</h>end thy boughs, O tree of glory!
Thy relaxing sinews bend;
For awhile the ancient rigour,
That thy birth bestowed, suspend;
And the King of heavenly beauty
On thy bosom gently tend!

<h>T</h>hou alone wast counted worthy
This world's ransom to uphold;
For a shipwrecked race preparing
Harbour, like the ark of old;
With the sacred blood anointed
From the smitten Lamb that rolled.

<h>T</h>o the Trinity be glory
Everlasting, as is meet;
Equal to the Father, equal
To the Son, and Paraclete:
Trinal Unity, whose praises
All created things repeat.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Deliver me from my enemies, O my God.
<r>℟.</r> And defend me from them that rise up against me.
cae21b2193:
<h>Capitulum Hymnus Versus</h>
<r>Jer 11</r>
<c>T</c>u autem, Dómine Sábaoth, qui júdicas juste, et probas renes et corda, vídeam ultiónem tuam ex eis: tibi enim revelávi causam meam, Dómine Deus meus.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>V</c>exílla Regis pródeunt:
Fulget Crucis mystérium,
Quo carne carnis Cónditor
Suspénsus est patíbulo.

<h>Q</h>uo vulnerátus ínsuper
Mucróne diro lánceæ,
Ut nos laváret crímine,
Manávit unda et sánguine.

<h>I</h>mpléta sunt quæ cóncinit
David fidéli cármine,
Dicens: In natiónibus
Regnávit a ligno Deus.

<h>A</h>rbor decóra et fúlgida,
Ornáta Regis púrpura,
Elécta digno stípite
Tam sancta membra tángere.

<h>B</h>eáta, cujus bráchiis
Sæcli pepéndit prétium,
Statéra facta córporis,
Prædámque tulit tártari.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>A</c>broad the regal banners fly,
Now shines the cross’s mystery;
Upon it Life did death endure,
And yet by death did life procure.

<h>W</h>ho, wounded with a direful spear,
Did, purposely to wash us clear
From stain of sin, pour out a flood
Of precious water mixed with blood.

<h>T</h>hat which the prophet-king of old
Hath in mysterious verse foretold,
Is now accomplished, whilst we see
God ruling nations from a tree.

<h>O</h> lovely and refulgent tree,
Adorned with purpled majesty;
Culled from a worthy stock, to bear
Those limbs which sanctifièd were.

<h>B</h>lest tree, whose happy branches bore
The wealth that did the world restore;
The beam that did that body weigh
Which raised up hell’s expected prey.

<r>The following verse is said on bended knee.</r>

<h>O</h> Cross, our one reliance, hail!
This holy Passiontide avail
To give fresh merit to the saint,
And pardon to the penitent.

<h>B</h>lest Trinity, salvation’s spring,
May every soul thy praises sing;
To those thou grantest conquest by
The holy cross, rewards apply.
Amen.

<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>A</c>uróra lucis rútilat,
Cælum láudibus íntonat,
Mundus exsúltans iúbilat,
Gemens inférnus úlulat:

<h>C</h>um Rex ille fortíssimus,
Mortis confráctis víribus,
Pede concúlcans tártara,
Solvit a pœna míseros.

<h>I</h>lle qui clausus lápide
Custodítur sub mílite,
Triúmphans pompa nóbili,
Victor surgit de fúnere.

<h>S</h>olútis jam gemítibus,
Et inférni dolóribus,
Quia surréxit Dóminus,
Respléndens clamat Ángelus.

<h>Q</h>uǽsumus, Auctor ómnium,
In hoc pascháli gáudio,
Ab omni mortis ímpetu
Tuum defénde pópulum.

<h>G</h>lória tibi Dómine,
Qui surrexísti a mórtuis,
Cum Patre et Sancto Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
2f37d98191:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>O</c> thou, the heavens' eternal King,
Creator, unto thee we sing,
With God the Father ever One,
Co-equal, co-eternal Son.

<h>T</h>hy hand, when first the world began,
Made in thine own pure image man,
And linked to Adam, sprung from earth,
A living soul of heavenly birth.

<h>A</h>nd when by craft the envious foe
Had marred thy noblest work below,
Clothed in our flesh, thou didst restore
The image thou hadst made before.

<h>S</h>o that thou might redeem man
Whom thou hadst made
And us to God might thou wouldst unite
Through thy union with the flesh.

<h>O</h>nce wast thou born of Mary's womb;
And now, new-born from out the tomb,
O Christ, thou bidd'st us rise with thee
From death to immortality.

<h>E</h>ternal Shepherd, thou dost lave
Thy flock in pure baptismal wave,
That mystic bath, that grave of sin,
Where ransomed souls new life begin.

<h>R</h>edeemer, thou for us didst deign
To hang upon the Cross of pain,
And give for us the lavish price
Of thine own blood in sacrifice.

<h>G</h>rant, Lord, in thee each faithful mind
Unceasing paschal joy may find;
And from the death of sin set free
Souls newly born to life by thee.

<h>T</h>o Thee Who, dead, again dost live,
All glory, Lord, Thy people give;
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.

b0af01a035:
<h>Capitulum Hymnus Versus</h>
<r>Rom 6</r>
<c>C</c>hristus resúrgens ex mórtuis jam non móritur, mors illi ultra non dominábitur. Quod enim mórtuus est peccáto, mórtuus est semel: quod autem vivit, vivit Deo.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>S</c>ermóne blando Angelus
Predíxit muliéribus:
In Galilǽa Dóminus
Vidéndus est quantócius.

<h>I</h>llæ dum pergunt cóncite
Apóstolis hoc dícere,
Vidéntes eum vívere,
Osculántur pedes Dómini.

<h>Q</h>uo ágnito discípuli
In Galilǽam própere
Pergunt vidére fáciem
Desiderátam Dómini.

<h>C</h>laro pascháli gáudio
Sol mundo nitet rádio,
Cum Christum jam Apóstoli
Visu cernunt corpóreo.

<h>O</h>sténsa sibi vúlnera,
In Christi carne fúlgida,
Resurrexísse Dóminum
Voce faténtur pública.

<h>R</h>ex Christe clementíssime,
Tu corda nostra pósside:
Ut tibi laudes débitas
Reddámus omni témpore.

<h>Q</h>uǽsumus, Auctor ómnium,
In hoc pascháli gáudio,
Ab omni mortis ímpetu
Tuum defénde pópulum.

<h>G</h>lória tibi Dómine,
Qui surrexísti a mórtuis,
Cum Patre et Sancto Spíritu
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Gavísi sunt discípuli, allelúja.
<r>℟.</r> Viso Dómino, allelúja.
851426682b:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>Rom 6</r>
<c>K</c>nowing that Christ rising again from the dead, dieth now no more, death shall no more have dominion over him. For in that he died to sin, he died once; but in that he liveth, he liveth unto God.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>T</c>he morn had spread her crimson rays,
When rang the skies with shouts of praise;
Earth joined the joyful hymn to swell,
That brought despair to vanquished hell.

<h>H</h>e comes victorious from the grave,
The Lord omnipotent to save,
And brings with him to light of day
The saints who long imprisoned lay.

<h>V</h>ain is the cavern’s three-fold ward —
The stone, the seal, the armed guard;
O death, no more thine arm we fear,
The Victor’s tomb is now thy bier.

<h>L</h>et hymns of joy to grief succeed,
We know that Christ is risen indeed;
We hear his white-robed angel’s voice,
And in our risen Lord rejoice.

<h>W</h>ith Christ we died, with Christ we rose,
When at the font his name we chose;
Oh, let not sin our robes defile,
And turn to grief the paschal smile.

<h>T</h>o God the Father let us sing,
To God the Son, our risen King,
And equally let us adore
The Spirit, God forevermore.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> The disciples were glad, alleluia.
<r>℟.</r> When they see the Lord, alleluia.

<c>A</c>d cenam Agni próvidi,
Et stolis albis cándidi,
Post tránsitum maris Rubri,
Christo canámus Príncipi.

<h>C</h>uius corpus sanctíssimum,
In ara crucis tórridum,
Cruóre ejus róseo
Gustándo vívimus Deo.

<h>P</h>rotécti Paschæ véspere
A devastánte Angelo,
Erépti de duríssimo
Pharaónis império.

<h>I</h>am Pascha nostrum Christus est,
Qui immolátus agnus est:
Sinceritátis ázyma,
Caro ejus obláta est.

<h>O</h> vere digna hóstia,
Per quam fracta sunt tártara,
Redémpta plebs captiváta,
Réddita vitæ prǽmia.

<h>C</h>onsúrgit Christus túmulo,
Victor redit de bárathro,
Tyránnum trudens vínculo,
Et Paradísum réserans.

<h>Q</h>uǽsumus, Auctor ómnium,
In hoc pascháli gáudio,

Tuum defénde pópulum.

acae1fa516:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>Rom 6</r>
<c>K</c>nowing that Christ rising again from the dead, dieth now no more, death shall no more have dominion over him. For in that he died to sin, he died once; but in that he liveth, he liveth unto God.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>A</c>t the Lamb’s high feast we sing
Praise to our victorious King,
Who hath washed us in the tide
Flowing from his piercèd side.

<h>P</h>raise we him whose love divine
Gives the guests his blood for wine,
Gives his body for the feast,
Love the victim, love the priest.

<h>W</h>here the paschal blood is poured,
Death’s dark angel sheathes his sword;
Israel’s hosts triumphant go
Through the wave that drowns the foe.

<h>C</h>hrist, the Lamb whose blood was shed,
Paschal victim, paschal bread;
With sincerity and love
Eat we manna from above.

<h>M</h>ighty victim from the sky,
Powers of hell beneath thee lie;
Death is conquered in the fight;
Thou hast brought us life and light.

<h>N</h>ow thy banner thou dost wave;
Vanquished Satan and the grave;
Angels join his praise to tell —
See o’erthrown the prince of hell.

<h>P</h>aschal triumph, paschal joy,
Only sin can this destroy;
From the death of sin set free,
Souls re-born, dear Lord, in Thee.

<h>H</h>ymns of glory, songs of praise,
Father, unto thee we raise;
Risen Lord, all praise to thee,
Ever with the Spirit be.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Stay with us, O Lord, alleluia.
<r>℟.</r> Because it is towards evening, alleluia.

<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>I</c>esu nostra redémptio,
Amor et desidérium,
Deus Creátor ómnium,
Homo in fine témporum:

<h>Q</h>uæ te vicit cleméntia,
Ut ferres nostra crímina,
Crudélem mortem pátiens,
Ut nos a morte tólleres!

<h>I</h>nférni claustra pénetrans,
Tuos captívos rédimens,
Victor triúmpho nóbili
Ad dextram Patris résidens.

<h>I</h>psa te cogat píetas,
Ut mala nostra súperes
Parcéndo, et voti cómpotes
Nos tuo vultu sáties.

In hoc pascháli gáudio,
Ab omni mortis ímpetu
Tuum defénde pópulum.

f9941239a1:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>H</c>ail, thou who man's Redeemer art,
Jesu, the joy of every heart;
Great Maker of the world's wide frame,
And purest love's delight and flame:

<h>W</h>hat nameless mercy thee o'ercame,
To bear our load of sin and shame?
For guiltless, thou thy life didst give,
That sinful erring man might live.

<h>T</h>he realms of woe are forced by thee,
Its captives from their chains set free;
And thou, amid thy ransomed train,
At God's right hand dost victor reign.

<h>L</h>et mercy sweet with thee prevail,
To cure the wounds we now bewail;
Oh, bless us with thy holy sight,
And fill us with eternal light.

<h>P</h>aschal triumph, paschal joy,
Only sin can this destroy;
